figures.Fig20.1a: Figure 20.1 Energy level diagram of hydrogenation of cyclohexenes and benzene (PDF page 61). Original figure archived as c12-chem-ch20-fig-hydrogenation (drawn for this lesson after the printed figure; not the textbook's picture). The printed figure shows the levels out of place (the 1,3-cyclohexadiene and benzene labels above the 240 kJ/mol line, cyclohexene above the 208 line); drawn with each level at its value (correct).

findings: The book says benzene's heat of hydrogenation is '158.5 kJ/mol lower than expected' and, in the next paragraph, '152 kJ/mol lower than the theoretical value'; 360 - 208 = 152, which the lesson uses.
A short definition of resonance is added for the learning outcome.
Figure 20.1 (energy levels) prints the 1,3-cyclohexadiene and benzene levels above the 240 kJ/mol line and cyclohexene above the 208 line; the redrawn figure places every level at its value.
